description: Import cards by clicking a base64url-encoded link, skipping the paste textarea entirely

tasks.title: Base64url encode/decode utility module
tasks.description: As a developer, I want a pure base64url encode/decode module so that card batch JSON can be safely embedded in and extracted from URL hash parameters.
acceptanceCriteria: encode(jsonString) produces a URL-safe base64 string (standard base64 with + → -, / → _, padding stripped)
decode(str) returns the original string for any valid encoded input
decode(str) returns null for malformed base64 input
decode(str) returns null for valid base64 that decodes to invalid UTF-8
Round-trip encode→decode is lossless for large payloads (1000+ card JSON)
Module has no DOM or DB dependencies — pure JS
Unit tests cover: round-trip, malformed input, empty string, large payload
tasks.notes: Depends on nothing. This is the foundation for UI-002.

tasks.title: URI import trigger in deck-view
tasks.description: As a user, I want the app to detect a cards param in the URL hash on load so that I land directly on the deck-selection step with my cards pre-loaded, ready to confirm.
acceptanceCriteria: When the app loads with #deck?cards=<valid-encoded-payload>, the confirm panel (deck-selection step) opens immediately — the paste textarea step is skipped
The confirm panel shows the correct card count from the decoded payload
When the payload is invalid (malformed base64 or fails parseCardBatch validation), an error message is shown and the normal deck view is rendered
After a successful import, the cards param is stripped from the hash (URL becomes #deck or #deck?id=<deckId>)
If the app is already open and a hashchange fires with a cards param, the import panel opens correctly without a full page reload
No regression: absence of cards param renders the normal deck view as before
tasks.notes: Depends on UI-001. Reuses existing parseCardBatch() and the confirm panel (renderStep2). No new UI panel needed.

tasks.title: Cancel URI import returns to normal deck view
tasks.description: As a user, I want to cancel a URI-triggered import so that I can abandon it without any cards being added and end up in a usable app state.
acceptanceCriteria: A cancel button is visible on the confirm panel when triggered via URI import
Tapping cancel adds no cards to the database
After cancel, the hash is rewritten to remove the cards param
After cancel, the user lands on the normal deck view (last opened deck or default)
tasks.notes: Depends on UI-002. May be a small addition to the existing cancel/close behavior in the confirm panel.

tasks.title: Confirm panel shows skipped-card count for URI import
tasks.description: As a user, I want to see how many cards were skipped due to validation errors during a URI import so that I know if my import was partial.
acceptanceCriteria: When the URI payload contains some invalid cards, the confirm panel shows both the valid card count and the skipped count
The display matches the existing skipped-card UI used in the paste import flow
When all cards are valid, no skipped count is shown (same as paste flow)
tasks.notes: Depends on UI-002. Likely zero new UI work if the existing renderStep2() already surfaces parseErrors — just needs verification.
